candidate.title: PB-seq
candidate.scope: The PB-seq row of the supplied Illumina schematic: purification of genomic DNA, shearing, in vitro binding to a DNA-binding protein, partition of bound and free fragments, and extraction of selected DNA. The row terminates at DNA; the sequencing interface and meaning of read abundance are clarified by the supplied catalogue and Guertin et al. primary paper. The adjacent 5-C and Pu-seq rows and the clipped UMI-4C material are contextual, separate workflows. PB-seq is protein/DNA binding followed by high-throughput sequencing; the HSF experiment is its cited implementation, not a second target method. The graph retains the drawn Purify DNA then Shear DNA order. Protein-capture chemistry is specified only for the cited HSF implementation; the generic protein icons do not establish applicability of that chemistry to all DNA-binding proteins. The introductory PB-seq icon is descriptive, not an extra transformation; no pooling or iterative enrichment branch is drawn. The excluded unbound fraction is an endpoint, not a second sequenced library.

operations.mechanism: The diagram depicts bound/free partition without naming the capture chemistry. In the cited HSF implementation, C-terminal 3xFLAG-tagged HSF enables capture on ANTI-FLAG M2 affinity gel followed by specific FLAG-peptide elution of HSF and associated DNA. This explains the isolation interface for that implementation; it does not establish a universal capture reagent for every DNA-binding protein.
operations.information_effect: Partition enriches DNA associated with the binding protein, and only the retained fraction proceeds to extraction. Enrichment does not eliminate all background or ensure recovery of low-affinity sites; the HSF paper reports finite detection range.

method_scopes.rationale: The title, row label and candidate collection heading all identify PB-seq. All five operations belong to this one row. The initial chromatin icon supplies DNA; binding is assayed after purification on naked DNA. The HSF primary paper confirms in vitro binding, selection and sequencing. No iterative SELEX or ChIP-seq workflow is added. For the HSF implementation, the tagged-protein input and the FLAG selection mechanism form a supported local interface within PB-seq; the generic method name is not a claim that every implementation shares that reagent. The caption hybridize is interpreted as protein-DNA association from the paper, not as nucleic-acid probe hybridization. The collection page also lists an Ozer et al. SELEX review as reference 321. Only this secondary listing is available for that review, so it is background context and supports no additional PB-seq operation or target. The actual card-listed method reference is Guertin et al.; its PB-seq association is assessed from supplied publication metadata and full text in pm_guertin.
